subject: Pilot certification path and acceptance checklist
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Emma Bryant <emma.bryant@healthscope.com>; Tom Keegan <tom.keegan@healthscope.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot certification path and acceptance checklist

Emma / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. As promised, I put together a one-page pilot certification path and an acceptance checklist to make the evaluation deterministic and to shorten the close timeline. Attached: MAP_v1.xlsx (mutual action plan + timeline). Key highlights below: 

- Objective: Verify Redwood inference meets HealthScope latency (p50 < 120ms) and quality (top-line correctness > 95% on the 200-case prompt set) for the triage workflow.
- Exit gates (hard):
  - Security: SOC2 report and network segmentation confirmation.
  - Performance: sustained 95th-percentile latency under agreed load profile.
  - Accuracy: pass rate >= 95% on curated acceptance checks.
- Acceptance tests (examples):
  1) Latency sweep at 10, 25, 50 RPS (p50/p95/p99)
  2) End-to-end business QA: 200 prompts, blind scoring by three SMEs
  3) Data handling: show retention path and KMS encryption for test artifacts
- Canary plan: 1-week canary (2 hosts) followed by progressive ramp (2x, 4x) if no regressions
- Timeline: kickoff next Monday (Aug 16), 2-week execution window, sign-off target Aug 30.

Please review the attached MAP_v1 and call out any missing acceptance tests you need (security, legal, or clinical QA). I copied Lauren to coordinate test owners and CS handover.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: MAP_v1.xlsx (stated content: milestone table, owners, and timeline)

Subject: Re: Pilot certification path and acceptance checklist — technical acceptance checks

Mateo / Lauren —

I sketched a compact tech acceptance checklist that ties directly to the MAP milestones. Attached: tech-acceptance-checks.md (short runbook + test commands). Highlights:

- Performance tests:
  * JMeter scenario for 10/25/50 RPS with synthetic prompts (script included).
  * Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 token latency, GPU utilization, and token cost per 1k tokens.
- Functional correctness:
  * Blind scoring harness: results exported to CSV with anonymized prompts.
  * Triage-specific metrics: precision/recall on label set; pass threshold 95%.
- Failure modes & rollback triggers:
  * If p95 > 500ms for two consecutive runs => automatic rollback to previous model variant.
  * If blind scoring falls below 90% on control set => hold ramp and engage ML ops.
- Security & data handling:
  * End-to-end TLS validation for all endpoints (scripted).
  * Retention: test artifacts stored in customer-owned bucket for 30 days, then rotated.

I recommend adding a short canary smoke test (10 prompts, end-of-day) that CS runs for the first 3 days post-deploy.

-Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Attachment: tech-acceptance-checks.md (runbook with commands and pass/fail criteria)
